task.description: Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's output for REQ-036. Read lib/letflow/design/promotion_plan.md independently (not CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary). Read REQ-036's full entry in docs/requirements.yaml first. Pay particular attention to Section 9 (Open questions) -- CODE-DESIGNER flagged 4 real data-model gaps: no permission-string concept in REQ-020's model (9.1, no built-in default for opts[:permission_checker]), no tenant production/test classification column (9.2, flagged default: classify-all-as-:test via opts[:tenant_classifier]), variable_schemas never ported (9.3, safe always-nil default), process_definitions.version free-form text with unconfirmed > semantics (9.4, flagged numeric-else-lexicographic fallback). Independently judge whether each of these is a legitimate flagged default (stated, reasoned, not scope creep) versus a silent guess or an unacceptable resolution -- do not just accept CODE-DESIGNER's own framing without checking the actual source files it cites (lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex, tenant_role.ex, group.ex, tenant.ex, lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex).
acceptance_criteria: Every one of REQ-036's 6 acceptance criteria maps to a concrete design element with no TBD/deferral
All 3 modules' function signatures fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases)
Error handling shape stated explicitly ({:ok,_}|{:error,_} tags, not left implicit)
No implementation code present (no .ex code bodies -- signatures and type shapes only)
Independently verify the 4 open-question defaults in Section 9 against the actual source files cited, not just CODE-DESIGNER's summary of them
Independently verify the permission_checker default (9.1) is genuinely NOT a silently-invented enforcement mechanism -- it must have no built-in default per the design

result.summary: Independently read REQ-036's full requirement.yaml entry (lines 1639-1714, all 6 acceptance_criteria) and the full lib/letflow/design/promotion_plan.md (726 lines) directly, not CODE-DESIGNER's handoff summary. Independently re-read the 5 source files the design's Section 9 open questions cite: lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex, tenant_role.ex, group.ex, tenant.ex, and lib/letflow/definitions/process_definition.ex. Verified each of the 4 flagged data-model gaps against those files directly: (9.1) confirmed RoleRegistry is exactly a (role_name -> group_id) binding registry (list_roles/0, upsert_role/2, resolve_role_in_tx/1) with no permission-string concept, no user->role assignment table, and no group-membership table anywhere in the codebase (Group's own moduledoc states full group-membership modeling is out of scope) -- the design's opts[:permission_checker] correctly carries NO built-in default (Section 3.2 step 1 states this explicitly) rather than silently inventing enforcement; (9.2) confirmed Tenant's schema is exactly {slug, display_name, status(:active|:migrating), idp_realm_id} with no kind/type/environment column -- the classify-everything-as-:test default is stated with explicit reasoning (reject-nothing is the only default that doesn't fail closed on data never designed to answer the question, no production deployment exists yet) and flagged for REVIEWER/REQ-ANALYST follow-up, not hidden; (9.3) confirmed via grep across lib/ and priv/ that no variable_schemas table or process_definitions.variable_schema column exists anywhere -- the always-nil fetcher default is correctly characterized as an objectively-true current fact rather than a guessed business rule; (9.4) confirmed process_definitions.version is field(:version, :string) with only validate_length/2 (no numeric/format constraint) in process_definition.ex -- the numeric-else-lexicographic version_greater?/2 fallback is stated as an explicit flagged resolution with a note for REVIEWER to re-confirm and for TEST-DESIGNER to pin both cases. Ran the full standard gate checklist: all 6 REQ-036 acceptance criteria map to a named, concrete design element in Section 10's table with no TBD/deferral language (grepped for 'TBD'/'to be implemented'/'to be determined' -- zero matches outside the doc's own closing sentence referencing the absence of such placeholders); all 3 modules' (PromotionPlan, PromotionConflict, PromotionDigest) function signatures are fully specified with explicit @spec types, and every error case is enumerated as a named atom/tuple in a dedicated @type (compute_error, conflict_error) -- compute_plan_digest/1's bare String.t() and verify_digest/2's boolean() return (no {:ok,_}/{:error,_} wrapper) are explicitly justified as pure/cannot-fail functions citing the existing Graph.validate_graph/1 precedent per the backend guide's own carve-out, not an omission; cross-module dependencies are listed explicitly in Section 7 (dependency diagram plus prose for each module); grepped the entire design doc for def/defp/do-block/Repo.insert-update-delete patterns and confirmed zero implementation code -- all fenced blocks are @type/@spec declarations, prose algorithm steps, or an ASCII dependency diagram, matching the validator-approved precedent this doc itself cites (req033-snapshot-store.md, req024-event-type-registry.md). No failed checks found. PASS.
